sections.h2: Which Tonawanda this covers and who collects the tax
sections.html:
This guide covers the Town of Tonawanda in Erie County, the northern inner-ring suburb of Buffalo. It is not the separate City of Tonawanda to the north, so check which one appears on your bill. The Town Assessor's Office, at 716-877-8811, sets values and runs exemptions and grievances. Tax payments go through the Town Clerk's office and an online payment portal.

The town includes the Village of Kenmore, and the two together are often called Ken-Ton. A Kenmore address can carry a village tax on top of the town and county bills, so look for a village line on your bill.

  • Town of Tonawanda Assessor: values, STAR questions, exemptions, grievance applications.
  • Town Clerk's Office: in-person partial payments on weekdays.
  • Erie County Clerk, 25 Delaware Avenue, Buffalo: small claims assessment petitions.

sections.h2: Due dates for the three Tonawanda bills
sections.html:
The Town issues three separate bills, each with its own due date and last payment date. The county and town bill is due February 15 with a last payment date of June 30. The school bill is due October 16 with a last payment date of November 30. The village bill is due July 3 with a last payment date of November 1. Your own bill shows the dates for the cycle you are in.

Town of Tonawanda tax collection calendar
BillCoversDueLast payment date
County and TownJanuary 1 to December 31February 15June 30
School (Ken-Ton and Sweet Home)July 1 to June 30October 16November 30
VillageJune 1 to May 31July 3November 1

Part of the town lies in each of two school districts, Ken-Ton and Sweet Home, so the school bill you get depends on where the house sits.

County and town tax grows by a step every two weeks after the due date: 1.5 percent from February 19 to March 2, 3 percent from March 3 to 16, 4.5 percent from March 17 to 31, 6 percent from April 1 to 15 and 7.5 percent from April 16 to 30. School tax carries 7.5 percent for October 15 to 31 and 9 percent for November. Village tax carries 7.5 percent for July and another 1.5 percent for each month after.

You can pay a tax bill online, and the convenience fee depends on the method. A credit card costs 2.45 percent, a Visa debit card is a flat $3.95, other bank debit cards cost 1.50 percent and an electronic check is a flat $1.75. Electronic checks take about two weeks to process, so avoid one close to a deadline. The Town keeps none of these fees, since the web service provider collects them.

Partial tax payments cannot be made online. They are taken in person only, by cash, check or charge card, at the Town Clerk's Office, open weekdays from 8:30 in the morning until 4:00 in the afternoon.

The Town's rate page lists these 2025 homestead totals: 35.481651 for county and town tax outside the village and 24.476354 inside the village. The county line alone is 15.404260, and the Town of Tonawanda line is 20.077391. Homestead is the Town's word for owner-occupied residential property.

  • School tax for 2025/2026: Ken-Ton 59.1567004 and Sweet Home 45.787477 for homestead property.
  • Village homestead tax: 40.342600 for 2025.
  • Equalization rate: a 21 percent level of assessment for 2025.

A 21 percent ratio means assessed values run well below market. When you weigh a grievance, compare your assessment with that ratio and with recent sales, not with the full market price.

The Town and the Village of Kenmore offer exemptions for limited-income seniors, military service, disabled persons with limited incomes, volunteer firefighters and ambulance workers, nonprofits and clergy, plus business investment exemptions under RPTL 485-a and 485-b. New York State runs Basic and Enhanced STAR directly, so the Assessor's Office no longer takes STAR applications. Every owner-occupied house is eligible for STAR.

Owners with military service can choose one of two exemptions. The alternative exemption (RPTL 458-a) covers wartime service or an expeditionary medal, and the Cold War exemption (RPTL 458-b) covers service in that period. Either one applies only to county, city, town and village taxes and not to school district or special district taxes. The first application must be filed by March 1, because the exemption is not automatic.

If you cannot find a tax return or proof of income, the Assessor's Office can advise on the non-filer worksheets the Town provides for senior and disabled applicants. Call 716-877-8811 to ask which form fits you.

sections.h2: How to challenge a Tonawanda assessment
sections.html:
Start with an informal review between February 1 and April 1. Then file a formal application for the Board of Assessment Review, which hears complaints on Grievance Day, May 25 in 2027. Applications are available at the Assessor's Office from May 1. To schedule a hearing, call 716-877-8811 after May 2, or file for a non-hearing review by 9 p.m. on Grievance Day.

Residential challenges use form RP 524 plus the Board's residential information sheet with comparable sales in section 2. If the Board leaves you unsatisfied, a Small Claims Assessment Review petition costs $30 and must be filed by July 30 with the Erie County Clerk. You qualify only if you own and live in a one-, two- or three-family home, filed a timely complaint with the Board and ask for no bigger reduction than you sought there. Prepare at least eight copies.

The taxable status date is March 1, and exemption applications are due the same day.

sections.h2: What a Tonawanda seller needs before closing
sections.html:
Call the Building Department at 716-877-8801 for a certificate of compliance for the storm water system, because you need one to sell your property. The inspection generally covers the sump pump and its electric line, footing drains, yard drains and downspouts. Book it early so a failed item does not delay closing.

Permit records for the house are available from the Building Department only from 1965 on, since earlier plans were destroyed. The Town's deferred-payment loan programs also matter at sale. Under the Residential Rehabilitation loan, the balance becomes due when the house is sold or the deed changes, and the loan is secured by a mortgage filed with the Erie County Clerk. First-time homebuyer loans have the same trigger.

Owner-occupancy is 72.2 percent, the median owner-occupied value is $213,900 and median gross rent is $1,098. The July 2025 population estimate is 70,853.

faqs.q: Is Tonawanda town the same as Tonawanda city?
faqs.a: No. The Town of Tonawanda is a separate municipality in Erie County, and the City of Tonawanda lies to its north. Check which one appears on your tax bill.

faqs.q: Can I pay part of my Tonawanda tax bill online?
faqs.a: No. Partial payments are only taken in person at the Town Clerk's Office on weekdays, with a 4:00 p.m. close.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day in the Town of Tonawanda?
faqs.a: Tuesday, May 25, 2027, the fourth Tuesday of the month. Applications are available at the Assessor's Office from May 1.

faqs.q: How much does a Tonawanda small claims assessment petition cost?
faqs.a: The filing fee is $30, and it may be refunded if you prevail. The petition goes to the Erie County Clerk by July 30.

faqs.q: Must I schedule an inspection before selling in the Town of Tonawanda?
faqs.a: Yes, a certificate of compliance for the storm water system. Call the Building Department at 716-877-8801 to schedule it.
